Daniel Kokotajlo
Daniel Bendisi Kokotajlo
[
1
]
is an
artificial intelligence
(AI) researcher. He was a researcher in the governance division of
OpenAI
from 2022 to 2024,
[
2
]
and currently leads the
AI Futures Project
.
[
3
]
Biography
Kokotajlo studied at the
University of Notre Dame
, where he graduated with a BA in philosophy in 2014.
[
4
]
[
1
]
He went on to study philosophy in graduate school at the
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
, where he obtained an MA in 2017 under the supervision of John Thomas Roberts.
[
5
]
During his PhD study in philosophy at
Chapel Hill
, he was a recipient of the 2018–2019 Maynard Adams Fellowship for the Public Humanities.
[
6
]
In 2022, he became a researcher in the governance division of OpenAI.
[
2
]
Kokotajlo is one of the organizers of a group of OpenAI employees that claimed the company has a secretive and reckless culture that is taking grave risks in the rush to achieve
artificial general intelligence
(AGI).
[
7
]
[
8
]
When he resigned in 2024, he refused to sign
OpenAI's non-disparagement clause
, which could have cost him approximately $2 million in equity.
[
2
]
As of May 2024, Kokotajlo confirmed he retained the vested equity.
[
9
]
[
10
]
In June 2024, he, with other former OpenAI employees, signed a letter arguing that top frontier AI companies have strong financial incentives to avoid oversight, and calling for a "right to warn" about AI risks without fear of reprisal and while protecting anonymity.
[
11
]
In 2021, Kokotajlo wrote a blog post named "What 2026 Looks Like". In 2025,
Kevin Roose
commented that "A number of his predictions proved prescient."
[
12
]
[
3
]
He cofounded and leads the
AI Futures Project
, a nonprofit based in
Berkeley, California
which researches the future impact of artificial intelligence. In April 2025, the organization released
AI 2027
, a detailed forecast scenario predicting rapid progress in the automation of software development and AI research, followed by AGI. It laid out a scenario in which fully autonomous AI agents will be better than humans at "everything" around the end of 2027, imagining its impacts on the economy, domestic politics and international relations.
[
3
]
In November 2025, Kokotajlo clarified that his AGI median estimate had shifted to the 2030s.
[
13
]
[
14
]
AI 2040: Plan A
, a follow up to
AI 2027
presenting a more optimistic scenario, was published in July 2026.
